sections.html:
In the far south of Alabama, Foley is a Baldwin County city that anchors part of the Daphne-Fairhope-Foley metro area. Its best-known crossing is where U.S. Route 98 meets Alabama Highway 59. ZIP codes are 36535 and 36536, and the area code is 251.

Population went from 4,003 in 1980 to 7,590 in 2000, then 14,618 in 2010 and 20,335 in 2020. The 2025 estimate is 30,354. In 2020 the census tallied 8,799 households and 9,911 housing units, of which 11.2 percent sat empty. Owner vacancy was 2.4 percent against 10.3 percent for rentals. Residents had a median age of 48.5, and 28.6 percent were 65 or older, so some owners may be weighing a move or an estate sale.

Rapid growth puts new construction and older houses in front of the same buyers. Vacancy counts also take in second homes and rentals, whose owners face different choices than people living in their house full time.

sections.h2: OWA and the McKenzie Street corridor
sections.html:
The Poarch Band of Creek Indians owns and runs OWA, a 520-acre resort and entertainment destination. It opened in 2017 near the South McKenzie Street commercial corridor, with a shopping and dining area called Downtown OWA, an amusement park and a water park, Tropic Falls, whose first phase opened in June 2022.

Attractions like this bring jobs, traffic and short-term visitors. An investor may value a house near McKenzie Street differently than a family hunting for a quiet block, so say clearly where yours sits.

County rules, not a city district, set attendance zones here. Foley High School takes grades 9 to 12 and Foley Middle School takes grades 7 and 8. The K-6 elementary schools are Foley Elementary, Florence B. Mathis Elementary, Magnolia Elementary and Swift Consolidated Elementary. Parents ask about zoning before they make an offer, so be ready to send them to the county school office.

Most trips here go by car on U.S. 98 and Highway 59. The Baldwin Regional Area Transit System, called BRATS, runs a countywide dial-a-ride service. A house near the main roads and shops is simpler to market than one at the end of a long rural lane.

sections.h2: Deed tax and recording in Baldwin County
sections.html:
Transfers carry a state tax of 50 cents on every $500 of value, spelled out in Alabama Code 40-22-1, and the probate office charges a separate recording fee. A form with the true sale price goes in with the deed. Holding that proof back after the office asks can cost $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is larger.

  • Filing happens with the judge of probate in the county where the property lies.
  • Your sales contract says which side pays the tax, and it is normally settled at closing.
  • The deed is drafted, and the title checked, by an attorney or title agent.

sections.h2: Property tax on a Foley house
sections.html:
Every taxable parcel except public utilities is assessed by the county. The lien attaches October 1, the bill is due on the following October 1, and late status begins after December 31.

A mid-year sale normally splits the bill by days of ownership. See whether this year's bill is already paid before you pick a closing date.

sections.h2: Paperwork to gather before a Foley sale
sections.html:
Three papers settle most early questions: your recorded deed, the newest tax bill and any mortgage statement. Foley deeds are filed at the Baldwin County probate office.

DocumentWhy a buyer asks for itWhere to get it
Deed or trust paperworkShows who owns the houseYour files or the probate office
Lender payoff figureShows what must be cleared at closingYour lender
Names of others on titleHeirs or a former spouse may need to signProbate records or your attorney
Utility and insurance detailsNeeded if the house is emptyYour accounts

Any lien or ownership gap will surface during the title search. Hearing about it now beats hearing about it on signing day.

sections.h2: What a Foley closing looks like
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, the title search starts. The examiner reads the public record for liens, tax balances and ownership problems, and reports anything that must be cleared before the deed can pass. If a mortgage is open, the lender supplies a payoff figure.

At the closing table you sign the deed and the settlement statement. The statement shows the price, any payoff, the tax split and what comes to you. The deed then goes to the Baldwin County probate office. Bring photo ID and every key, remote and garage opener.

If you live out of town, ask whether you can sign by mail or at a title office near you. Many sales are handled without a trip back to Foley.

sections.h2: If you owe on the house
sections.html:
A mortgage or past-due tax does not stop a sale in Foley. The lender sends a payoff figure, the closing agent pays it out of your proceeds, and the lien is released as the deed changes hands. The same step clears any unpaid property tax, so the buyer starts with a clean title.

Ask for the payoff and the tax balance before you list or sign. With both figures in hand you can see what would be left for you and weigh a quick cash sale against a slower listing.

sections.h2: Selling a Foley rental or second home
sections.html:
Because so many local units are rentals or second homes, a Foley buyer will ask how the property has been used. Have the lease, rent history and any deposit records ready, and say whether the tenant plans to stay or leave.

A cash buyer can purchase a house with tenants in it or an empty one. Check the lease for notice terms before you set a closing date.

You can list on the open market, sell it yourself or accept cash. A listing may reach more people, though it brings showings, repairs and a need for a buyer who qualifies for a loan.

  • Listing means prepping the house, waiting for offers and haggling after the inspection.
  • Going it alone saves the commission, but the paperwork and buyer screening are yours.
  • Cash Home Buyers purchases as-is, so nothing needs repair or a deep clean for showings.

Heirs, landlords with problem rentals and owners of houses that need work often pick cash, since it shortens the path from deciding to selling.

An empty house sells fine. Keep insurance and utilities on until closing, and have the deed and tax bill ready. A cash buyer looks at the property as it stands and needs no staging. If heirs share the title, all of them will have to sign.

Cash offers usually land below a polished retail sale, yet they cut out repair bills, showings and waiting. Compare what you would keep after those costs.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Foley house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer takes the house as it stands and builds repair costs into the price. A closing professional can tell you what to disclose.

faqs.q: How is deed tax set in Baldwin County?
faqs.a: The state rate is 50 cents per $500 of value, and the county probate office adds a recording fee.

faqs.q: When is the property tax bill due in Foley?
faqs.a: It is due October 1 and becomes delinquent after December 31. A sale normally splits the bill.

faqs.q: Who handles the closing for a Foley sale?
faqs.a: Normally a title agent or attorney. The probate office files the deed but will not draft it.

faqs.q: Will a cash offer be higher than a listing price?
faqs.a: Usually it is lower than a polished retail price, but it skips repairs, showings and delays. Compare what you would net.
